messages.subject_clean: Using PXD015169 data from PRIDE in MSstats
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to load a data set from the PRIDE data base into R using MSstats. The accession number for PRIDE is in the subject line, and here is the paper reference: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01871-9
In the "technical validation" section of the paper, the authors state that they used MaxQuant for analysis, and that "there are several software tools that accept MaxQuant output files directly, such as MSstats".

My problem is that the files from PRIDE have .raw, .mzid, and .MGF extensions. Those file extensions do not match the flat text file extension in the example code in the MSstats vignette for the MaxQtoMSstatsFormat function. How can I import PXD015169 data into R? I don't really care what package I use - I just want to get the data into R. Here's what I have thus far:

library(rpx)
# Need to create a cache
my_cache <- BiocFileCache::BiocFileCache(tempfile())
my_cache
px <- PXDataset2("PXD015169", cache = my_cache)
pxfiles(px, 61)
>> Output at the end of this email due to its length.  Which files fit into the evidence.txt, proteinGroups.txt and annotation.csv files for entry into R using MSstats?

I do not have access to MaxQuant. All I have access to are the files in PRIDE.
Thanks,
MMc

The proteins with a pvalue of 0, log FC of infinity, and say "one condition missing", cannot be modeled because we have no measurements for one of the conditions in the comparison. We will not impute these missing values as we have no evidence of where the missing values should be.

For the remaining ones, I think the pvalues are not 0, but are very small and excel is rounding them to 0 because it cannot handle how small they are. You'll see the proteins at the bottom of your list are not actually 0 but very small. I would assume the others have an even lower pvalue and excel just can't show them.

Best,
Devon
